newsitem.title: USA: Job guarantees not necessarily a problem for Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Job guarantees not necessarily a problem for Chrysler.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. President Robert Lutz said Wednesday the guarantees Ford Motor Co. set in its new labour pact would not likely be a problem for Chrysler if the company has the flexibility to adjust workforce levels at individual plants.

Lutz, speaking to reporters at a convention for Chrysler dealers here, said he was optimistic the company would be able to reach an equitable settlement with the United Auto Workers union for a new labour contract covering the automaker's 66,000 hourly employees.
The current contract expired Sept. 14, but the UAW extended the deadline.

Ford, the first of the Big Three to reach a tentative agreement with UAW, agreed to keep 95 percent of its current UAW hourly workforce over the life of the three-year contract, unless the company was hit by a severe industry downturn.

Lutz said maintaining jobs for 95 percent of Chrysler's hourly workers over the past five years would not have caused a problem because Chrysler has added about 13,000 new hourly UAW jobs in the United States during that period.

In the future, he said Chrysler's ability to support a 95 percent employment guarantee would depend largely on contract language and Chrysler's flexibility to shift employees from plant to plant in order to maintain efficiencies.
"If it's defined by little individual pockets and we have no ability to blend (workforces), that would be unacceptable," he said.
Lutz denied earlier statements by UAW President Stephen Yokich that Chrysler cares more about its suppliers than its workers, calling Yokich's statements "campaign rhetoric."
He said he has not heard whether Chrysler will be chosen as the second bargaining target by the UAW.
Meanwhile, Chrysler announced the company and its dealers will spend a combined $2 billion on advertising for the 1997 model year.
Included in that total will be a new corporate advertising campaign with the theme "Great Cars," which will emphasise the company's design and engineering capabilities.
Chrysler is also launching a new advertising campaign for the Chrysler brand under the slogan "What's new in your world?" that seeks to promote the product line as youthful and forward-looking.

Chrysler told dealers that advertising in most markets will emphasise the Neon Expresso package, which will include the more powerful dual overhead cam engine, at a price of $12,770, which is $300 more than the Neon Highline model.
Other ads shown to dealers included a lease rate of $299 a month for the 1997 Sebring convertible, and a $359 a month lease rate for the 1997 LHS sedan. Other terms of the leases were not disclosed.
